newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS- Korea borrowers look to London.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS- Korea borrowers look to London.

text.p: News that South Korean borrowers are looking further afield for funds added some interest to a dull Asian debt market on Thursday.
Korea Development Bank (KDB) and Korea Electric Power Corp (Kepco) plan to issue sterling-denominated bonds, South Korea's finance and economy ministry said.
A Kepco official said the company would issue 150 million sterling straight bonds this month. Roadshows will be held in London next week.
KDB will issue sterling-denominated bonds equivalent to 320 million.
The Korean quasi-sovereigns are sophisticated borrowers that have tapped a number of international markets, including the U.S. Yankee, Japanese Samurai and Australian Kangaroo markets.

Korea Telecom overnight launched a US$200 million Yankee bond. The 7.625 percent bond due 2007 was priced and 98.994 to yield 7.771 percent, or 90 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries. Salomon Brothers was lead manager.
Standard and Poor's Corp has assigned a AA-minus rating to the Korea Telecom bonds.
Korea Mobile also is expected to tap the U.S. markets soon.
Closer to home, Coryo Merchant Bank is expected to launch a US$30 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue pending approval by South Korea's finance ministry.
The 364-day paper is seen paying an all-in return of around 85 basis points. Sumitomo Finance is tipped as lead manager.
Elsewhere in Asian, China Construction Bank's floating rate note issue appears to be faring well in the secondary market. The US$200 million five-year notes were launched and closed on April 1.
The notes, which were priced to give a fixed re-offer yield of 33 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate, reportedly were trading at 31-33 basis points today.

As expected, Chase Manhattan Asia wil run the books on China Investment Bank's US$100 million floating rate note issue. Other lead managers are Bayerische Landesbank Hong Kong, Daiwa Securities Hong Kong, HSBC Markets and Standard Chartered Bank.
Roadshows for Thailand's Yankee bond start next week. The bond will start at US$500 million in size and is expected to have 10- and 30-year tranches. Lehman and Salomon are leads.
